purpose: Proposed source-class -> EyeCU-class mapping. NOTHING IS REMAPPED. This file records a proposal and the evidence behind it.
method: Every mapping was confirmed by looking at rendered crops of that class (experiments/external_data_audit/contact_sheets/<SID>_class<N>_*.jpg). Instance frequency and box aspect ratio were used to form the hypothesis; the crops decided it. Frequency alone cannot separate goalkeeper from referee -- both are rare humans -- so no numeric class was assigned without visual confirmation.

rows.evidence: S1_class0_Ball.jpg -- footballs on grass, correct object
S1_class1_Player.jpg -- outfield players in both kits
rows.review_reason: TAXONOMY GAP, not a naming problem. S1 has no goalkeeper class, so goalkeepers are inside 'Player'. Importing this as EyeCU 'player' actively teaches the detector that goalkeepers are players, contradicting EyeCU's own labelling rules and the 431 goalkeeper instances already in TRAIN.

S2.note: French class names. This is the only source whose four classes align 1:1 with EyeCU's four with no taxonomy gap.

rows.evidence: French 'ballon' = ball; S2_class1_Ballon.jpg shows footballs, though many boxes are visibly oversized
rows.review_reason: Correct object, poor geometry -- see annotation quality report

rows.evidence: French 'gardien (de but)' = goalkeeper; S2_class2_Gardien.jpg shows keepers in goalmouths in distinct kits, several diving
French 'joueur' = player; S2_class3_Joueur.jpg shows outfield players
S3_class0_football.jpg -- 'football' here means the ball, not the sport

rows.review_reason: Same taxonomy gap as S1: no goalkeeper class, so goalkeepers are folded into 'player'.

S4.note: Numeric class names carry no semantics. The order is the alphabetical ball/goalkeeper/player/referee convention Roboflow produces, confirmed visually class by class.

rows.evidence: S4_class0_0.jpg -- footballs. Smallest class (median 4x7 px), <=2 per image, 230 instances.
S4_class1_1.jpg -- keepers in distinct bright kits standing in goalmouths. 0.68/image, 185 instances, human aspect 3.4:1.
S4_class2_2.jpg -- outfield players. 19.97/image, 5431 instances -- the only class that can be the field population.
S4_class3_3.jpg -- black-kit officials, several on the touchline. 2.29/image, consistent with a 3-official crew.
single-class export; S5_ball.jpg confirms the object
rows.review_reason: The class maps cleanly, but the DATASET does not: every image contains unlabelled players. See the partial-annotation verdict.

S6.note: Same numeric convention as S4, confirmed independently on this source's own crops.

rows.evidence: S6_class0_0.jpg -- footballs, median 10.3x11.0 px, aspect 1.00 (square, as a ball is). 0.63/image.
S6_class1_1.jpg -- keepers in the goalmouth in distinct kits, one mid-save. 0.44/image.
S6_class2_2.jpg -- Barcelona and opposition outfield players. 13.96/image.
S6_class3_3.jpg -- yellow-shirted La Liga officials, 24/24 correct. 1.29/image.

cross_source_findings.unknown_or_irrelevant_classes: none -- every declared class maps to one of EyeCU's four
cross_source_findings.consequence: S1 and S3 cannot supply the goalkeeper class and would inject goalkeeper-as-player conflicts. S5 supplies only ball.
